analysis: All three changed files are documentation or changelog only: changelog.d/model-download-cancellation-completion.md (added, 3 lines), docs/architecture/model-registry.md (new paragraph at head lines 26-34, date bump) and docs/developer/test.md (new 'Download completion ownership' section, date bump). No executable source is in the supplied batch. The docs describe a Swift fix in StreamingFileDownloadDelegate and ModelDownloader: the first terminal result is retained until the continuation attaches, so cancellation no longer hangs. Cancellation closes the writer and keeps the resumable .part file, and CancellationError propagates without retry so the artifact writer lease unwinds. Relevant threat IDs are T-012 and A-004 (model weights integrity) and T-016/T-010 (availability). The documented behavior does not weaken any threat-model control. Weight verification, manifest hashing and on-demand verification are described as unchanged. The only integrity-related point is that resumable .part files are preserved on cancellation. Whether a resumed .part file is re-verified against the manifest hash before use, and whether the continuation is resumed exactly once, can only be checked in the actual Swift source (StreamingFileDownloadDelegate.swift, ModelDownloader.swift), which is not in this batch. Those claims are unverified here. The source change and its tests should be reviewed in whichever batch contains them, notably for double-resume or lock-ordering errors and for the completeness of .part verification on resume. The test doc states the tests use temporary directories and do not resume network tasks or load weights, with no security impact. No findings. The deeper-review flag is set only for the unseen implementation.
